historical_record.description: Building of a model yacht lake and reservoir was under way, with $11,904.17 spent that year.
Under the name Spreckels Lake, the lake took a further $11,845.97 in labour, clay and hardware, with a walk, a drive and grounds around it.

The Park Commissioners proposed an artificial lake of about six acres east of Thirty-sixth Avenue, about four feet deep and holding at least 7,800,000 gallons, filled with water pumped by windmill from new wells near the ocean, with low wharves at each end for people sailing miniature yachts.

Spreckels Lake covered seven acres on the north side of the park between Thirty-first and Thirty-sixth Avenues, 100 feet above tide, with wooded margins and a driveway around it; miniature yachts were sailed there to test the models. Windmills lifted its water from wells near the ocean.
